description: Weekly, because a personal dashboard has no cadence to keep up with, and each run costs a full tsc, lint, test and vite build. Batching a week of bumps into one wake-up keeps the queue readable.

Nothing automerges: a merge to master deploys to plot.hani.fyi in the same CI run, so an automerged bump is a production deploy with nobody looking. The suite is pure logic and there are no DOM or component tests, so a green run says the bundle builds and the arithmetic holds — not that a chart still renders.

packageRules.description: vite.config.ts strips this package's series autoloaders by regex against its compiled output, matching a literal `const seriesModuleLoaders = {...}`. A replace that finds nothing returns the code unchanged, so a release reshaping that declaration leaves the plugin doing nothing and the autoloaders back in the bundle — a silent size regression rather than a build failure. A bump here wants `npm run analyze` read against the committed analyze.json. Ungrouped so that check has one PR to happen in.

One thing in two packages: eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7's recommended config is the React Compiler's own rule set, so a gap between them changes which violations get reported without changing which exist. A compiler bump also moves the bailout count, and nothing in CI can see a bailout — `this` and `??=` compile fine and quietly lose memoization. The check is the logger procedure in AGENTS.md, run by hand, so both move in one PR and one pass covers them.
